Its Application Summary states that 'Site Layer 1, LLC (Site Layer 1) is proposing to construct a data center powered by a natural gas–fired electrical power generation development (the “Project”), on private land in Hidalgo and Grant Counties', that 'The anticipated data center size is approximately 800 megawatts (MW), with on-site gas generation providing approximately 300 MW', and that the generation project area is 7,214.4 acres wholly in the Grant County parcel; the plant is 32 Wärtsilä 20V34SG gas engines of about 9.4 MW each with SCR and oxidation catalysts (SIC 4911). Section 1 lists Site Layer 1, LLC as plant owner and operator, status 'Not Constructed', anticipated construction start Q1 2027, completion Q3 2028 and start-up Q4 2028, and gives the facility location as latitude 31.980569, longitude -108.511384 (UTM zone 12, NAD 83: 735,145 E, 3,540,987 N; County Grant; elevation 4,540 ft; 4.9 miles north-east of Playas; land status Private). The modeling report says the Project 'consists of a natural gas–fired electrical generation and data center development' and its preliminary layout (Figure 2, 'Data Center & Gas Engine Site Plan') draws four data-centre buildings beside the engine hall. The public-notice letters to counties of 27 August 2026 announce the application 'for the construction of its data center powered by natural-gas fired electrical power generation facility' at 31.980165 N, 108.511324 W.

us-or-wa-p5-prineville-cc-20261013-packe.summary: The Public Works staff report for item 7 asks the council to approve Resolution 1654 so that the City can enter a development agreement with Apple, Inc. for administrative oversight of the 'PRZ-06 Offsite Utility Expansion Project', which coordinates 'the construction of utility improvements necessary to serve Apple's eastern campus expansion'. Its background states that 'Apple's initial development plan included the expansion of the easter[n] portion of its campus', which 'requires offsite utility improvements to serve the development of this area' (16-inch domestic water, 12-inch non-potable water, 21-inch sanitary sewer, 12-inch reclaimed/industrial wastewater, 8-inch gravity and 4-inch pressure sewer lines, bored under Highway 126 in 54-inch and 24-inch steel casings). Recital A of the attached agreement states that Apple 'owns and operates a data center campus on real property located within City, as described in Exhibit A', and recital B that the project is the offsite utility infrastructure 'needed to serve the eastern portion the User's campus PRZ 06 development area within Prineville, Oregon'. Exhibit A (Parametrix, 'System Improvements at Points of Connection') labels the APPLE CAMPUS and shows the PRZ06 offsite lines reaching its north side and running along its eastern edge, with pressure tables for campus phases 1B, 2B and buildout. Apple reimburses the City's costs up to USD 8,803,435.44 plus an 8.5 percent administrative fee; the City is to strive for Final Completion of the utility project by 31 March 2028 and to reserve 350 gpm of future water delivery (in addition to 99 gpm current delivery) until Apple calls for it or 30 September 2028. This dated government record names Apple's eastern campus expansion in the PRZ 06 development area of the existing Prineville campus as a planned development; it does not describe the buildings, floor area, power or IT capacity, permits or construction start of the expansion, and the utility schedule and water reservation are forecasts, not observations.

additions.site_identity_review: The City of Prineville's Resolution 1654 packet identifies the expansion as the 'eastern portion' of Apple's own Prineville data-centre campus, the 'PRZ 06 development area', and its development agreement describes that campus as the real property within the City on which Apple owns and operates a data center campus (recital A, Exhibit A). This is the same campus, the same agreement and the same City record that establish the existing Atlas site curated:apple-prineville-data-center-campus (vcc-site-9bb771ea13115bdd8091; project 'Apple Prineville Data Center Campus — existing operations', whose status evidence is this packet). Exhibit A labels the APPLE CAMPUS (and the Exhibit B pipeline map hatches it east of Prineville Airport) and shows the PRZ06 offsite lines reaching its north side and running along its eastern edge. The expansion is therefore a further phase of the existing campus, not a separate physical site; its buildings are not yet described.

status.summary: The City of Prineville's packet for its 13 October 2026 council meeting (generated 8 October) presents Resolution 1654 and a development agreement under which the City procures and oversees the 'PRZ-06 Offsite Utility Expansion Project', 'utility improvements necessary to serve Apple's eastern campus expansion'. The staff report states that 'Apple's initial development plan included the expansion of the easter[n] portion of its campus', which requires these offsite water, non-potable water, sanitary sewer and industrial-wastewater lines, and recital B of the agreement describes the project as the infrastructure 'needed to serve the eastern portion the User's campus PRZ 06 development area'. The council adopted the resolution unanimously on 13 October 2026. This dated government record announces Apple's planned eastern campus expansion in the PRZ 06 development area of its existing Prineville data-centre campus. It does not describe the expansion's buildings, floor area, power or IT capacity, and no land-use approval, building permit or site work for the expansion is asserted; the utility contract's 31 March 2028 Final Completion target and the 350 gpm future water reservation (until 30 September 2028) are forecasts and reservations, not observations, and the offsite utility works themselves are not treated as a construction stage of the data-centre expansion.

additions.successor_review: Checked on 27 October 2026: the City of Prineville AgendaCenter (captured 27 October 2026 UTC) lists after the 13 October packet only the Planning Commission brief of 20 October (no land-use item; Planning Director update on data-centre-funded water and wastewater line extensions; next meeting 17 November 2026) and the 27 October council packet, whose draft 13 October brief records the unanimous adoption of Resolution 1654 and contains no later Apple item. A recheck capture of the 13 October packet returned byte-identical content. Crook County's building department publishes permits only through the state ePermitting portal (not queried). No site plan, building permit, construction start, cancellation or change to the expansion was found, so the status stays announced as of 8 October 2026.
